description.short_caption: MRI of the left forearm (sagittal T2-weighted view).
description.detailed_description: This is a sagittal T2-weighted MRI of the left forearm. The image shows hyperintense signal areas within the bone marrow, suggestive of edema or infiltration. The surrounding soft tissues appear relatively preserved, with no obvious fluid collections or masses. The cortical bone and joint spaces are visible, and there is no clear evidence of fracture or dislocation.
visible_findings: no evidence of fracture or dislocation

Case_14005/figure1.jpg.source_caption: MRI of left wrist (axial T2-weighted view) with low-signal masses.

description.short_caption: Axial T2-weighted MRI of left wrist showing low-signal masses.
description.detailed_description: This axial T2-weighted MRI of the left wrist demonstrates multiple low-signal intensity masses within the soft tissue. The surrounding structures, including tendons and bones, appear intact. The low-signal areas suggest dense material, possibly fibrous tissue or calcifications. The image provides good contrast between the masses and surrounding tissues, aiding in their identification.
visible_findings: low-signal intensity masses in soft tissue
clear delineation of structures on T2-weighted imaging

description.short_caption: Tissue removed during surgical debridement, showing grape-like clusters.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a collection of small, pink, grape-like nodules on a blue background. The nodules are irregularly shaped and appear uniform in color and texture. A ruler is visible in the lower right corner, providing a size reference, with the nodules measuring approximately 1-3 cm in diameter. The appearance is consistent with tissue removed during surgical debridement, potentially representing granulomatous or infectious material.
